editorial:
Imagine having a job where you literally burn money for a living. That is exactly what Gilbert does at the Bank of France. He is a nice, simple guy who loves his wife and son, but he is a bit too trusting for his own good. He used to be in a rock band with his brother-in-law, Marc, who is the total opposite of him. Marc is a smooth talker and a liar who sees Gilbert as an easy target. He tricks Gilbert into believing that a huge amount of money went missing and that Marc is in serious danger because of it. It is a funny but stressful setup that shows how far a person will go when they think they are saving a family member.

You will really enjoy how the tension builds as Gilbert struggles with his conscience before finally giving in to the plan. The acting is great, especially the chemistry between the two leads, making the betrayal feel personal. While the pace slows down a bit in the middle, the payoff is worth it. If you love stories about the little guy getting some revenge, you need to see this.
endingExplained: After Gilbert realizes Marc lied to him and used him just to rob the bank, he decides he has had enough. Instead of staying quiet, he goes to the police and gives them the exact date and time of the planned robbery. The police set a trap, and Marc is caught red-handed during the heist. Gilbert gets the last laugh, proving that even the most naive person can be smart when they are pushed too far.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heist comedies and stories about revenge.
